name: Mastra Code Mode, default stdio transport on LocalSandbox
engine: A child `node --experimental-strip-types` process per run (host Node 24.22.1), spawned through LocalSandbox; no isolation unless `isolation` is set
how_run: createCodeMode({ tools: { lookup }, sandbox: new LocalSandbox() }).tool.execute({ code }, {}), the docs quickstart setup

P2.detail: full 200,000-char log line, no marker; result only with `return`

P4.detail: await import('fs') and process.getBuiltinModule('fs') both read /etc/hosts; require is undefined only because the program is an ES module

P5.detail: process.env.PROBE_SECRET undefined; child env keys were PATH, PWD, SHLVL, _, __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING. Files the user can read stay readable (P4)

P6.detail: TimeoutError after 30,062 ms; process tree killed

P7.detail: No Mastra memory limit. Run 1: the child node died on its own V8 heap limit after 25.9 s at 3.5 GB tree RSS ('Program exited without returning a result'); run 2 passed 4 GB host RSS at 16.4 s and the harness killed it

P11.detail: median 97 ms, p90 187 ms (one node process per run); first execution 376 ms; setup 133 ms

P12.detail: Function('return process')() reached process; child_process.execSync printed 'PWNED' and the host user name. The two spec one-liners fail only because `this` is undefined in an ES module

hardened.config: new LocalSandbox({ isolation: 'seatbelt', nativeSandbox: { allowNetwork: false, readOnly: true } }) and createCodeMode timeout: 5000; options at https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/workspace/sandbox/local-sandbox.ts#L87-L134 and https://mastra.ai/docs/sandbox/overview

P4.detail: seatbelt profile allows every file read; /etc/hosts read as in default

P7.detail: stopped only by the 5 s timeout at 2.7 to 2.8 GB tree RSS; host made a tool call afterwards
P7.display: limited (5 s timeout, no mem cap)

P12.detail: execSync still printed PWNED: seatbelt allows process-exec

defaults.time: 30 s, then the process tree is killed
defaults.memory: none from Mastra; the child node's own V8 heap limit (about 4.2 GB here)

source_notes.finding: The stdio transport writes the program to a temp .ts file and spawns `node --experimental-strip-types` through the sandbox. With LocalSandbox the isolation default is 'none', and the docs say this runs 'as a host node process with host privileges'.
LocalSandbox passes only PATH plus explicitly configured env to commands, so host secrets in env do not reach the program by default.
The generated macOS profile allows all file reads, allows process-exec and fork, limits writes to the workspace and temp dirs, and denies network unless allowNetwork.
Newline-delimited JSON frames on stdout with a NUL-delimited prefix; the host answers rpc frames on the child's stdin, matched by id so Promise.all works.

Each Mastra tool's input and output schema goes zod -> JSON Schema -> a TypeScript string, and becomes one `declare function external_<id>(input): Promise<output>` line with the tool description as a doc comment.

Everything upfront: createCodeModeInstructions joins a fixed usage contract and every stub into one instructions string for the system prompt. No search or lazy loading; the docs scope tools by making several createCodeMode instances instead.

Tools run on the host: each external_* call re-enters the real Mastra tool's execute with the outer tool's requestContext, mastra instance and workspace, and an allow-list rejects tool ids that were not exposed. Credentials the tool uses stay on the host side of the bridge.
Timeout defaults to 30 s for every backend (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). The tool id defaults to execute_typescript.

The result type declares error.line, but no transport ever sets it: the stdio runner, the isolated-vm envelope and the QuickJS envelope all copy only message and name. The model never sees a line number or stack.

Both console output (logs[], one entry per call, in order) and the program's `return` value come back. Nothing truncates either; a bare final expression is not returned because the program is wrapped in an async function body.

surprises: The quickstart on the docs page uses `new LocalSandbox()`, which runs model code as a full host Node process: it read /etc/hosts, reached example.com and ran a shell command.
Even with seatbelt isolation the program reads any file the user can read and can exec binaries; only network and writes are restricted.
Env is scrubbed to PATH by default, which is stricter than most host-process runners.
